notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH, 2026-09-30 (D-15, the outermost `low` cadence band), after reading the one proposal that named this id — proposals/eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-10-15.from-eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-30.json, filed by the 09-30 sibling lane's adjacency sweep on 2026-09-15. Its title and attribution rationale (same-day as saudi-east-west-pipeline-repair-window-close-2026-10-15; off-cadence 12:00 ET vs the standard 10:30 ET) are adopted, then honestly UPDATED with what a D-15 session on the actual date can now measure that the proposer could not two weeks earlier. FIRST UPDATE — the turnaround seasonal is confirmed live, not projected: EIA's own weekly history (wpuleus3, re-fetched direct this session) shows utilization at 97.8% (wk ending 09-04, the proposer's base) already down to 94.0% (wk ending 09-18, the newest published print) — a -3.8pt move in two weeks, ahead of the 96.0 threshold the sibling ledger is tracking for its own wk-ending-09-25 print. Extending the same seasonal methodology two more weeks to the wk ending 2026-10-09 this event covers: historically utilization keeps declining from a comparable mid-September point in 27/33 years since 1993 (median further decline -3.2pts), landing this print's point estimates in an honest 86.7-93.0 range across two convergent methods — below 96.0 with very high confidence (as it has been in 32/33 years historically), but the exact trough level genuinely uncertain, which is why this ledger's forward test is framed as directional (continued decline) rather than pinned to a specific level. SECOND UPDATE, and it CUTS AGAINST the proposer's title framing: the Saudi East-West pipeline the proposer named as this date's hook has already substantially restarted — Reuters/Bloomberg/AGBI/OilPrice.com (all re-checked 2026-09-30) report the line restarted operations around 2026-09-22, building toward 4 mb/d, with full capacity still weeks out; Brent has fallen from the proposer's 106.01-108.80 range to ~96-97 intraday this session on the restart plus OPEC/IEA 2026 demand-forecast cuts. The 'same day as the repair window closes' framing is honestly narrower now: the shock has been unwinding for over a week already, so the print's context on 10-15 is a mostly-deflated premium and a demand-led selloff, not a live supply shock. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact stays `low` on the same grounds as both siblings: no house playbook is energy-keyed, no tracked symbol carries direct crude exposure, `symbols` is empty on purpose. ONE GENUINE NEW SIGNAL this session's own data turned up: distillate stocks show ZERO builds in the mid-September-to-early-October window across the last 10 years (0/10, 2016-2025) — unlike the coin-flip crude/gasoline pattern the 09-30 sibling found for its own three-week-earlier window — and 2026 distillate is still -12.7% y/y despite ticking up the last two prints, so the structural-tightness read from the September 2026 STEO (unchanged edition, re-confirmed current via the landing page 2026-09-30 — no October edition published yet) still holds.
